claims.text: Replacing EAM+TI with a TaVCrW-trained MTP+FEP workflow will reduce computational cost by more than 80% while maintaining sub-meV accuracy.
High-fidelity reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distribution by the MTP is the critical structural mediator enabling the method substitution.
The MTP will reproduce the vibrational density of states and atomic-displacement correlations in both liquid and solid TaVCrW.
Accurate reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distribution permits efficient FEP estimation of the solid-liquid free-energy difference without TI's slow convergence.
An MTP captures the complex many-body interactions of liquid TaVCrW that EAM does not capture accurately.
FEP requires fewer sampling windows than TI when the reference MTP is accurate.
The SRO contribution to TaVCrW solid-phase stability will be less than 1 meV/atom in the 2000-2400 K melting range.
SRO-related strengthening in MoNbTaW becomes negligible at 2000 K.
SRO stabilization is suppressed near melting because thermal entropy dominates the SRO energetic contribution.
Electronic-excitation or density-of-states gap effects may shift the TaVCrW melting point by approximately 10-20 K.
High-temperature magnetic fluctuations are likely negligible for TaVCrW.
A supercell containing more than 10,000 atoms is required to avoid finite-size effects and capture percolating SRO clusters.
Validation must cover 2000-2400 K because this range contains the TaVCrW melting transition and is where SRO is thermally suppressed.
The method is valid only if the MTP training set includes diverse TaVCrW liquid and high-temperature solid configurations.
TaVCrW is modeled initially as a bcc random solid solution at 0 K and then equilibrated at 2000-2400 K.
The predicted TaVCrW melting point is approximately 2250 ± 10 K.
The TaVCrW melting temperature will be calculated with an uncertainty below 5 K.
Baseline TOR-TILD calculations require more than 1000 CPU hours for similar systems.
Insufficient liquid configurations in the training set could cause high uncertainty in liquid-phase MTP accuracy.

The benchmark falsifies the method if the MTP+FEP and TOR-TILD free-energy results differ by more than 0.5 meV/atom, the cost reduction is below 80%, or the experimental melting point is missed by more than 20 K.

contradictions.description: The claimed sub-meV accuracy and less-than-5 K uncertainty conflict with the separate prediction of 2250 ± 10 K and acknowledged possible errors of 10-20 K from electronic excitations and 1-2 meV/atom from transferring the SRO assumption.
The SRO contribution is predicted to be below 1 meV/atom, while the uncertainty field states that transferring the MoNbTaW result may introduce a 1-2 meV/atom solid-free-energy error.

The rule describes a difference in calculated melting temperature as exceeding 0.5 meV/atom, conflating a temperature difference with a free-energy-per-atom threshold; these are distinct measured quantities unless an explicit thermodynamic conversion is supplied.
